summary: Harry P Williams Memorial Airport is a small general aviation facility serving Patterson, Louisiana, in the heart of the Bayou Region along the Atchafalaya Basin. The airport provides convenient access to the surrounding coastal communities, oil and gas industry operations, and recreational areas near the Atchafalaya Swamp. Named after a local civic leader, it primarily supports private aviation, flight training, and charter operations rather than scheduled commercial service.
faqs:
Q: Does Harry P Williams Memorial Airport offer commercial airline service?
A: No, PTN is a general aviation airport with no scheduled commercial flights; travelers typically use larger airports like Lafayette Regional or Baton Rouge Metropolitan for commercial service.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features runways, tie-downs, fuel services, and hangars suitable for small private aircraft and flight training.

Q: Can pilots fly in for fuel or transient parking?
A: Yes, the airport accommodates transient general aviation aircraft with available fuel and parking facilities.

Q: Is the airport used for any specialized operations?
A: It commonly serves helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft supporting the offshore oil and gas industry in the Gulf of Mexico region.
transport_tips: Since the airport has no scheduled commercial service, visitors typically fly in via private or charter aircraft, with ground transportation arranged in advance. Patterson is located along US Highway 90, approximately 30 miles south of Lafayette and roughly 90 miles west of New Orleans, making car rental the most flexible option upon arrival. Local taxi services and ride-sharing availability may be limited, so coordinating ground transport ahead of time is recommended.
local_tip: If you're flying into PTN for business in the oil patch or a fishing trip, time your arrival for daylight hours, as the surrounding bayou terrain and frequent low ceilings in coastal Louisiana can make evening approaches challenging for unfamiliar pilots.
